weights_license: checkpoint cards do not state a separate license; assumed Apache-2.0 alongside the code pending explicit confirmation

observed.input_contract: RGBA PNG with meaningful alpha, composited onto white; --no_rembg passed so InstantMesh's bundled rembg/u2net model is never downloaded or invoked
observed.checkpoint_gating: none -- both downloaded without any Hugging Face login/license-acceptance step

excluded_dependencies: rembg/u2net: importable (run.py imports it unconditionally) but never invoked at runtime because Darkness always passes --no_rembg
known_risks: This is a single low-effort smoke qualification (default 75 diffusion steps, no prompt/view tuning), not a blinded multi-generator quality benchmark.

IMPORTANT visual finding: fewer connected components (10) than TripoSG's baseline (17) does NOT mean higher visual quality here. Side-by-side comparison of the rendered diagnostics shows TripoSG's candidate is a clearly recognizable, correctly-oriented standing goblin despite its fragmentation, while this InstantMesh candidate is disorganized and reads as rotated/tumbled, much harder to recognize as a coherent standing character. Connected-component count is a structural metric, not a proxy for silhouette/identity quality.

The adapter passes --no_rembg and skips InstantMesh's own resize_foreground(0.85) framing step (normally paired with its internal rembg call); this may be under-preparing the input relative to what the model was tuned to expect and could partly explain the weaker visual result. Worth testing an owned foreground-crop/resize step before drawing final conclusions.
InstantMesh is an April 2024 architecture; independent 2026 comparisons place it a generation behind TRELLIS.2/Hunyuan3D on mesh quality generally.
The output is geometry-only (OBJ converted to GLB); a separate PBR/material path is required regardless.
Generated character bodies remain topology/detail targets until canonical fitting and deformation tests pass, same as every other geometry candidate.
